- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a price spike (forecast > history mean + 10%), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent 7-day average.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 10d true values before final output.
